title: A field-valued point in the image of a closed immersion factors through it
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], let $K$ be a field, and let $s:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ be a morphism whose unique image point is $i(z)$ for some $z\in Z$. Then there is exactly one morphism $s':\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ with $i\circ s'=s$, and the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ maps to $z$ under $s'.$

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 0356 (lemma-map-into-reduction: a morphism from a reduced scheme factors through a closed subscheme iff it does so set-theoretically), applied to Spec K; Definition Tag 01HK (closed immersion) and Lemma Tag 01L7 (immersions are monomorphisms) give uniqueness

mathlib_searches.query: a morphism from Spec K for a field whose image point lies in a closed subscheme factors uniquely through the closed immersion
mathlib_searches.results: IsClosedImmersion.lift (requires a kernel inclusion), IsClosedImmersion.lift_fac, Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField; no theorem converting the set-theoretic image condition for Spec K into the kernel inclusion

mathlib_searches.query: field-valued point factors through closed immersion when its image is in the closed image
mathlib_searches.results: SpecToEquivOfField and IsClosedImmersion.lift; neither states the reduced-source/set-theoretic factorization

mathlib_searches.query: AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.lift, Spec K, exists unique factorization
mathlib_searches.results: IsClosedImmersion.lift, lift_fac, isIso_lift; all require the scheme-theoretic kernel condition rather than only that the point lies in the image
ClosedImmersion.lean has lift only with a kernel inclusion; no reduced-source field-point factorization theorem in Mathlib
